extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, peer reviewers, and journal editors involved in animal (in vivo) research; also useful to ethical review boards, funders, institutions and learned societies
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist-style reporting guidelines for publications describing in vivo (animal) experiments, intended to ensure transparent, thorough, and reproducible reporting so readers and reviewers can evaluate methodological rigour. Applicable across species and stages of research (planning, conduct, manuscript writing, and review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist of information to include in publications describing animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARRIVE guidelines (Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments) are a checklist of information to include in publications describing animal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist to ensure manuscripts contain all relevant information about the study; the checklist is intended as an aide-memoire for manuscript preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report studies in enough detail to add to the knowledge base
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines ensure that studies are reported in enough detail to add to the knowledge base. Scientific publications reporting animal research often lack important information, limiting their utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting in adherence with ARRIVE 2.0 ensures transparent and thorough reporting, enabling readers and reviewers to scrutinise the research adequately, evaluate its methodological rigour, and reproduce the methods or findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient methodological detail for scrutiny, evaluation and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting should enable readers and reviewers to scrutinise the research, evaluate methodological rigour, and reproduce methods/findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods, sample sizes, analyses and other key methodological details are reported thoroughly so others can judge risk of bias and attempt replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include design and bias-minimisation information (planning-stage guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: During study planning the guidelines and accompanying Explanation and Elaboration document provide advice on experimental design, minimisation of bias, sample size and statistical analyses, helping researchers design rigorous and reliable in vivo experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ARRIVE guidance at the planning stage to inform design decisions (randomisation, blinding, sample size justification, appropriate statistical methods) that will later need to be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record important methodological information during conduct of the study
rubrics_metrics.description: During the conduct of a study the guidelines allow researchers to record important information about study methods, which will be needed later for manuscript preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of protocol details, deviations, animal characteristics, and implementation of design features (e.g., randomisation, blinding) so reporting is complete and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ARRIVE as an aide-memoire when writing the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing a manuscript the guidelines can be used as an aide-memoire to ensure the manuscript contains all relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check manuscript sections against the checklist to avoid omitting critical details required for interpretation and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ARRIVE when reviewing manuscripts to check availability of relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a manuscript the guidelines should be used to ensure all relevant information is available to evaluate the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors can apply the checklist to identify missing methodological or reporting elements that impede assessment of validity and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability across animal species and areas of biosciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARRIVE guidelines are relevant to any study involving live animals, from mammals to fish, as well as invertebrates, in any area of the biosciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the checklist principles across taxa and research areas, adapting specific item details as appropriate for species- or field-specific methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based, collaboratively developed guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARRIVE guidelines 2.0 and their Explanation and Elaboration were developed by an international working group with input from researchers, funders, editors, methodologists and statisticians, supplemented by surveys, a Delphi exercise and road-testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The development process supports the guidelines' authority; users can rely on them as consensus-based, prioritised items and expect them to be understandable to the main audience.
